q: 医生说我要在家休息___，不能去上班。
zh: 医生说我要在家休息三天，不能去上班。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ yào zài jiā xiū xi sān tiān bù néng qù shàng bān
en: The doctor says I have to rest at home for three days and can't go to work.
why: How long goes after the verb, so you need a length: 三天 is three days of rest. 三点 is a clock time and 三号 a date; neither can measure how long you rest.

q: 周末我打算好好睡___十个小时。
zh: 周末我打算好好睡十个小时。
py: zhōu mò wǒ dǎ suàn hǎo hǎo shuì shí gè xiǎo shí
en: This weekend I plan to get a good ten hours of sleep.
why: A plan has not happened yet, so no 了 sits between 睡 and the duration; 了 would make it finished, and 过 would make it a past experience, both clashing with 打算.

q: 我太累了，想在床上睡___。
zh: 我太累了，想在床上睡一会儿。
py: wǒ tài lèi le xiǎng zài chuáng shàng shuì yī huì r
en: I'm too tired; I want to sleep in bed for a little while.
why: 一会儿 is a short length of time and follows the verb. 遍 counts run-throughs and 趟 counts round trips, so neither measures how long you sleep.

zh: 我昨天睡了九个小时。
py: wǒ zuó tiān shuì le jiǔ gè xiǎo shí
en: I slept for nine hours yesterday.
why: The length of sleep follows 睡了, while 昨天 is a time-when and stays before the verb. 九个小时 cannot go in front of 睡.

zh: 他在医院住了一个星期。
py: tā zài yī yuàn zhù le yī gè xīng qī
en: He stayed in the hospital for a week.
why: The place 在医院 sits before the verb; the duration 一个星期 comes right after 住了 and cannot be moved in front of it.

zh: 她每天要在电脑前坐八个小时。
py: tā měi tiān yào zài diàn nǎo qián zuò bā gè xiǎo shí
en: She has to sit in front of a computer for eight hours every day.
why: Even in a habit, how long goes after the verb: 坐八个小时. 每天 is the when, and the place phrase 在电脑前 sits before 坐.

zh: 请你在这儿等十分钟。
py: qǐng nǐ zài zhè r děng shí fēn zhōng
en: Please wait here for ten minutes.
why: A request has no 了, but the duration 十分钟 still follows the verb 等; the place 在这儿 stays in front of it.

s: 我昨天晚上八个小时睡了。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang bā gè xiǎo shí shuì le
zh: 我昨天晚上睡了八个小时。
py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang shuì le bā gè xiǎo shí
en: I slept for eight hours last night.
why: 八个小时 says how long, so it must follow 睡了. Placed before the verb it is read as a time-when slot and the sentence breaks.

s: 他半个小时就写完了报告。
s_py: tā bàn gè xiǎo shí jiù xiě wán le bào gào
zh: 他半个小时就写完了报告。
py: tā bàn gè xiǎo shí jiù xiě wán le bào gào
en: He finished writing the report in just half an hour.
why: Trap: a duration before the verb with 就 means 'within that time', a different pattern from 'for how long', so the sentence is correct.

q: 我昨天看___两个小时电视。
zh: 我昨天看了两个小时电视。
py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn le liǎng gè xiǎo shí diàn shì
en: I watched TV for two hours yesterday.
why: A stretch finished yesterday takes 了 right after the verb, before the duration. 过 would mean having done it at some time, and 着 an ongoing state.

q: 我今天早上跑步___半个小时，累死了。
zh: 我今天早上跑步跑了半个小时，累死了。
py: wǒ jīn tiān zǎo shang pǎo bù pǎo le bàn gè xiǎo shí lèi sǐ le
en: I ran for half an hour this morning and was exhausted.
why: 跑步 is verb + object and cannot take a duration straight after it, so repeat the verb: 跑步跑了半个小时. 跑步了半个小时 is wrong.

q: 他每周打三个小时___球，身体很好。
zh: 他每周打三个小时的球，身体很好。
py: tā měi zhōu dǎ sān gè xiǎo shí de qiú shēn tǐ hěn hǎo
en: He plays ball for three hours a week and is in good health.
why: The duration sits before the object and is linked with 的: 三个小时的球. A habit takes no 了, and 着 cannot go there.

q: 老板昨天给客户打电话___了一个小时。
zh: 老板昨天给客户打电话打了一个小时。
py: lǎo bǎn zuó tiān gěi kè hù dǎ diàn huà dǎ le yī gè xiǎo shí
en: The boss was on the phone to the client for an hour yesterday.
why: With verb-object 打电话, repeat the verb and put 了 plus the duration on the second one. 打电话了了 or a bare 了 after 话 does not work.

q: 他来这家公司三年___，对工作已经很熟悉了。
zh: 他来这家公司三年了，对工作已经很熟悉了。
py: tā lái zhè jiā gōng sī sān nián le duì gōng zuò yǐ jīng hěn shú xī le
en: He has been with this company for three years and already knows the work well.
why: With the instant verb 来, time since follows the object and the sentence ends in 了. 过 and 着 do not express 'it has been three years now'.

zh: 她昨天打了两个小时球。
py: tā zuó tiān dǎ le liǎng gè xiǎo shí qiú
en: She played ball for two hours yesterday.
why: The duration goes between 打了 and its object 球. Verb + object + duration (打了球两个小时) is the English order and is wrong.

zh: 经理昨天开会开了三个小时。
py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān kāi huì kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí
en: The manager was in a meeting for three hours yesterday.
why: With the verb-object 开会, say the verb twice: 开会 first, then 开了 plus the duration. The duration cannot follow 会 directly.

zh: 她每天看一个小时的手机。
py: tā měi tiān kàn yī gè xiǎo shí de shǒu jī
en: She spends an hour on her phone every day.
why: The duration with 的 comes before the object: 看一个小时的手机. A habit takes no 了.

zh: 医生说我每天要游半个小时的泳。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ měi tiān yào yóu bàn gè xiǎo shí de yǒng
en: The doctor says I should swim for half an hour every day.
why: 游泳 splits around the duration: 游 + 半个小时的 + 泳. Putting the duration after 泳 would be the English order.

src: 他昨天游了一个小时泳。
src_py: tā zuó tiān yóu le yī gè xiǎo shí yǒng
task: Say it by repeating the verb.
zh: 他昨天游泳游了一个小时。
py: tā zuó tiān yóu yǒng yóu le yī gè xiǎo shí
en: He swam for an hour yesterday.
why: The verb-copy pattern puts the whole verb-object first, then repeats the verb with 了 and the duration. 了 goes only on the second verb.

src_py: jīng lǐ kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí huì
zh: 经理开了三个小时的会。
py: jīng lǐ kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí de huì
en: The manager was in a three-hour meeting.
why: 的 is optional but links a duration to the object that follows it: 开了三个小时的会. The order verb + duration + object stays the same.

src: 她昨天睡觉睡了九个小时。
src_py: tā zuó tiān shuì jiào shuì le jiǔ gè xiǎo shí
task: Put the duration before 觉 and add 的.
zh: 她昨天睡了九个小时的觉。
py: tā zuó tiān shuì le jiǔ gè xiǎo shí de jiào
en: She slept for nine hours yesterday.
why: 睡觉 can split: 睡了 + duration + 的 + 觉. This is the same meaning as repeating the verb, just built the other way.

s: 他昨天睡觉了十个小时。
s_py: tā zuó tiān shuì jiào le shí gè xiǎo shí
zh: 他昨天睡了十个小时。
py: tā zuó tiān shuì le shí gè xiǎo shí
en: He slept for ten hours yesterday.
why: 睡觉 is verb + object, so 了 and the duration attach to 睡, not after 觉. Say 睡了十个小时 or 睡了十个小时的觉.

s: 我们开了会三个小时。
s_py: wǒ men kāi le huì sān gè xiǎo shí
zh: 我们开了三个小时会。
py: wǒ men kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí huì
en: We were in a meeting for three hours.
why: 开会 is verb + object, so the duration cannot follow 会. Put it between 开了 and 会 (开了三个小时会), or repeat the verb: 开会开了三个小时.

s: 为了这个报告，我们小组昨晚加班加了四个小时。
s_py: wèi le zhè ge bào gào wǒ men xiǎo zǔ zuó wǎn jiā bān jiā le sì gè xiǎo shí
zh: 为了这个报告，我们小组昨晚加班加了四个小时。
py: wèi le zhè ge bào gào wǒ men xiǎo zǔ zuó wǎn jiā bān jiā le sì gè xiǎo shí
en: For this report our team worked overtime for four hours last night.
why: Trap: 加班 is verb + object, so the verb is repeated and 了 plus the duration go on the second 加. The sentence is correct.

q: 我在医院门口等___半天。
zh: 我在医院门口等了他半天。
py: wǒ zài yī yuàn mén kǒu děng le tā bàn tiān
en: I waited for him at the hospital entrance for ages.
why: A pronoun object goes right after the verb and 了, and the duration follows it: 等了他半天. 他了 misplaces 了, and 的 cannot be used with a pronoun.

q: 护士陪了___一个晚上，他才睡着。
zh: 护士陪了他一个晚上，他才睡着。
py: hù shi péi le tā yī gè wǎn shang tā cái shuì zháo
en: The nurse stayed with him all night before he finally fell asleep.
why: The pronoun 他 comes straight after 陪了, before 一个晚上. 的他 and 他的 turn the pronoun into a modifier and break the pattern.

q: 妈妈找了___一个上午，你去哪儿了？
zh: 妈妈找了你一个上午，你去哪儿了？
py: mā ma zhǎo le nǐ yī gè shàng wǔ nǐ qù nǎ r le
en: Mum has been looking for you all morning. Where did you go?
why: With a pronoun object the order is Verb + 了 + pronoun + duration: 找了你一个上午. Neither 你的 nor 的你 can sit there.

q: 培训部教了___整整两个星期，我们才学会这个新系统。
zh: 培训部教了我们整整两个星期，我们才学会这个新系统。
py: péi xùn bù jiāo le wǒ men zhěng zhěng liǎng gè xīng qī wǒ men cái xué huì zhè ge xīn xì tǒng
en: The training department taught us for two whole weeks before we mastered the new system.
why: The pronoun 我们 goes after 教了 and before the duration. Adding 的 before or after it makes it a possessive and the sentence falls apart.

zh: 老板等了你半天。
py: lǎo bǎn děng le nǐ bàn tiān
en: The boss waited for you for ages.
why: A pronoun object precedes the duration: 等了你半天. 等了半天你 puts the amount before the person and is wrong.

zh: 李医生照顾了我三个星期。
py: lǐ yī shēng zhào gù le wǒ sān gè xīng qī
en: Doctor Li looked after me for three weeks.
why: The pronoun 我 comes right after 照顾了 and the duration 三个星期 follows it.

zh: 同事帮了我一个下午。
py: tóng shì bāng le wǒ yī gè xià wǔ
en: A colleague helped me all afternoon.
why: With 我 as the object, the order is verb + 了 + 我 + duration, the reverse of 帮了一个下午的忙 where the object is a thing.

src_py: wǒ děng tā děng le bàn tiān
task: Say it without repeating the verb.
zh: 我等了他半天。
py: wǒ děng le tā bàn tiān
en: I waited for him for ages.
why: Instead of copying the verb, keep one 等了 and put the pronoun 他 directly after it, then the duration 半天.

s: 同事找了半天我。
s_py: tóng shì zhǎo le bàn tiān wǒ
zh: 同事找了我半天。
py: tóng shì zhǎo le wǒ bàn tiān
en: A colleague looked for me for ages.
why: A pronoun object must come before the duration. 找了半天我 reverses them, which Chinese does not allow with 我, 你 or 他.

s: 我等你等了一个小时。
s_py: wǒ děng nǐ děng le yī gè xiǎo shí
zh: 我等你等了一个小时。
py: wǒ děng nǐ děng le yī gè xiǎo shí
en: I waited for you for an hour.
why: Trap: the verb-copy pattern also works with a pronoun object (等你 then 等了一个小时), so this is correct.

q: 小王以前在这家公司工作了三年___，后来去了上海。
zh: 小王以前在这家公司工作了三年，后来去了上海。
py: xiǎo wáng yǐ qián zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò le sān nián hòu lái qù le shàng hǎi
en: Xiao Wang used to work at this company for three years, then went to Shanghai.
why: 以前 and 后来 show the three years are over, so only the 了 after the verb belongs. A second 了 would say he is still working there.

q: 上个月我感冒了一个星期___，现在已经好了。
zh: 上个月我感冒了一个星期，现在已经好了。
py: shàng gè yuè wǒ gǎn mào le yī gè xīng qī xiàn zài yǐ jīng hǎo le
en: Last month I had a cold for a week; I'm better now.
why: The cold is over, so the week is a finished stretch with one 了. The second 了 means 'so far, still going', which contradicts 已经好了.

q: 去年经理在国外出差了六个月___，今年已经回国了。
zh: 去年经理在国外出差了六个月，今年已经回国了。
py: qù nián jīng lǐ zài guó wài chū chāi le liù gè yuè jīn nián yǐ jīng huí guó le
en: Last year the manager spent six months abroad on business; this year he's back in China.
why: 去年 puts the six months entirely in the past, so one 了 only. Adding a final 了 would present the business trip as still going on.

zh: 我吃了三个月药了。
py: wǒ chī le sān gè yuè yào le
en: I have been taking the medicine for three months now.
why: Verb + 了 + duration + object, then a final 了 to say the three months run up to now and are not over.

zh: 他在这家医院工作了五年了。
py: tā zài zhè jiā yī yuàn gōng zuò le wǔ nián le
en: He has worked at this hospital for five years.
why: The second 了 goes at the very end and marks 'so far, and still going'. The place phrase stays before the verb.

zh: 我们已经等了他四十分钟了。
py: wǒ men yǐ jīng děng le tā sì shí fēn zhōng le
en: We have already been waiting for him for forty minutes.
why: The pronoun 他 comes before the duration, and the final 了 marks that the waiting is still going. 已经 sits before the verb.

src: 我在这个公司工作了三年。
src_py: wǒ zài zhè ge gōng sī gōng zuò le sān nián
task: Say you are still working there now.
zh: 我在这个公司工作了三年了。
py: wǒ zài zhè ge gōng sī gōng zuò le sān nián le
en: I have been working at this company for three years.
why: To say the three years run up to now and continue, add a second 了 at the end of the sentence, after the duration.

src_py: wǒ gǎn mào le sān tiān
task: Say it has lasted three days so far and is still going.
zh: 我感冒了三天了。
py: wǒ gǎn mào le sān tiān le
en: I have had a cold for three days now.
why: Adding a final 了 after 三天 turns a plain amount into 'three days so far, and still going'.

s: 我以前学了两年中文了，后来不学了。
s_py: wǒ yǐ qián xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le hòu lái bù xué le
zh: 我以前学了两年中文，后来不学了。
py: wǒ yǐ qián xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén hòu lái bù xué le
en: I studied Chinese for two years before, then gave it up.
why: The final 了 says the two years are still counting, but 以前 and 后来不学了 say it ended. Use one 了 only.

s: 我头疼了三天了。
s_py: wǒ tóu téng le sān tiān le
zh: 我头疼了三天了。
py: wǒ tóu téng le sān tiān le
en: I have had a headache for three days now.
why: Trap: two 了 are correct here. The first follows the verb and the second marks that the headache has lasted three days so far.

s: 去年夏天他在上海住了三个月了，秋天就回国了。
s_py: qù nián xià tiān tā zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān gè yuè le qiū tiān jiù huí guó le
zh: 去年夏天他在上海住了三个月，秋天就回国了。
py: qù nián xià tiān tā zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān gè yuè qiū tiān jiù huí guó le
en: Last summer he lived in Shanghai for three months, then returned to his country in autumn.
why: 去年夏天 puts the three months in a finished period, and 回国了 ends it. A final 了 after 三个月 wrongly says it is still going on.

s: 我跑步跑了三个月了，体重还是没有变化。
s_py: wǒ pǎo bù pǎo le sān gè yuè le tǐ zhòng hái shi méi yǒu biàn huà
zh: 我跑步跑了三个月了，体重还是没有变化。
py: wǒ pǎo bù pǎo le sān gè yuè le tǐ zhòng hái shi méi yǒu biàn huà
en: I've been running for three months now, but my weight hasn't changed.
why: Trap: in the verb-copy form the second 了 again goes last, so 跑了三个月了 is correct for 'three months so far, still running'.

q: 他___了，眼睛都红了。
zh: 他三天没睡觉了，眼睛都红了。
py: tā sān tiān méi shuì jiào le yǎn jīng dōu hóng le
en: He hasn't slept for three days, and his eyes are red.
why: For 'not done for a period', the duration goes before 没: 三天没睡觉了. There is no action after the verb to measure, so the duration cannot follow it.

q: 医生说我胃不好，我已经___没喝咖啡了。
zh: 医生说我胃不好，我已经一个多月没喝咖啡了。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ wèi bù hǎo wǒ yǐ jīng yī gè duō yuè méi hē kā fēi le
en: The doctor says my stomach is bad, and I haven't had coffee for over a month.
why: The length 一个多月 goes before 没. 一月 is January, a time-when, and 一点 is one o'clock or 'a bit'; neither is a length of time.

q: 小李___没来上班了，听说他病了。
zh: 小李一个星期没来上班了，听说他病了。
py: xiǎo lǐ yī gè xīng qī méi lái shàng bān le tīng shuō tā bìng le
en: Xiao Li hasn't come to work for a week; I heard he's ill.
why: The duration 一个星期 comes directly before 没, and the 了 belongs at the end of the clause. 一个星期了没来 splits the pattern; 三号 is a date.

q: 因为一直在出差，我已经___没回家吃过饭了。
zh: 因为一直在出差，我已经两个多月没回家吃过饭了。
py: yīn wèi yī zhí zài chū chāi wǒ yǐ jīng liǎng gè duō yuè méi huí jiā chī guo fàn le
en: Because I've been on business trips all along, I haven't eaten at home for over two months.
why: The length 两个多月 goes before 没. 两月 lacks the measure 个 that 月 needs for 'months', and 多两个月 is not a possible order.

q: 我已经___没跟老同学联系了，真想他们。
zh: 我已经很久没跟老同学联系了，真想他们。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng hěn jiǔ méi gēn lǎo tóng xué lián xì le zhēn xiǎng tā men
en: I haven't been in touch with my old classmates for a long time; I really miss them.
why: 很久 means 'a long time' and goes before 没. 很多 means 'many' and 很长 needs 时间 after it, so neither fits here.

zh: 我两天没吃饭了。
py: wǒ liǎng tiān méi chī fàn le
en: I haven't eaten for two days.
why: The duration 两天 goes before 没, and 了 at the end shows the situation still holds. 没吃饭两天 is not possible.

zh: 她很久没去医院了。
py: tā hěn jiǔ méi qù yī yuàn le
en: She hasn't been to the hospital for a long time.
why: 很久 goes before 没, not after the verb. The final 了 marks that the state of not going has lasted until now.

zh: 我已经一个星期没好好睡觉了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng yī gè xīng qī méi hǎo hǎo shuì jiào le
en: I haven't slept properly for a week now.
why: 已经 comes first, then the duration, then 没: the duration of not doing always sits in front of 没 and its verb.

zh: 我半年没去体检了。
py: wǒ bàn nián méi qù tǐ jiǎn le
en: I haven't had a medical check-up for half a year.
why: 半年 is the length of not doing it, so it goes before 没. Putting it after 去体检 would be the English order and is wrong.

task: Say he has not exercised for a month.
zh: 他一个月没锻炼了。
py: tā yī gè yuè méi duàn liàn le
en: He hasn't exercised for a month.
why: Turning a habit into 'not for a month' moves the duration in front of 没 and adds a final 了, since the situation is still true now.

src: 她每个星期都来办公室。
src_py: tā měi gè xīng qī dōu lái bàn gōng shì
task: Say she has not come to the office for two weeks.
zh: 她两个星期没来办公室了。
py: tā liǎng gè xīng qī méi lái bàn gōng shì le
en: She hasn't come to the office for two weeks.
why: The negative version puts 两个星期 before 没 来, not after the verb, and ends with 了 because the absence continues until now.

s: 我没喝水一天了。
s_py: wǒ méi hē shuǐ yī tiān le
zh: 我一天没喝水了。
py: wǒ yī tiān méi hē shuǐ le
en: I haven't had any water for a day.
why: For 'haven't done it for a period', the duration goes before 没: 一天没喝水了. Placing it after the verb and object is the English order.

s: 我没学两年，只学了一年。
s_py: wǒ méi xué liǎng nián zhǐ xué le yī nián
zh: 我没学两年，只学了一年。
py: wǒ méi xué liǎng nián zhǐ xué le yī nián
en: I didn't study for two years; I only studied for one.
why: Trap: here 没 denies the amount, so the duration stays after the verb. This is different from 'haven't done it for two years'.

s: 去年他有两个月没上班，在家养病。
s_py: qù nián tā yǒu liǎng gè yuè méi shàng bān zài jiā yǎng bìng
zh: 去年他有两个月没上班，在家养病。
py: qù nián tā yǒu liǎng gè yuè méi shàng bān zài jiā yǎng bìng
en: Last year he didn't go to work for two months and stayed at home recovering.
why: Trap: the duration 两个月 sits before 没 even in a past period, with 有 introducing it and no final 了. This is correct.

q: 这个药一天吃___，每次两片。
zh: 这个药一天吃三次，每次两片。
py: zhè ge yào yī tiān chī sān cì měi cì liǎng piàn
en: Take this medicine three times a day, two tablets each time.
why: 次 counts occasions of taking something, here three doses a day. 趟 is for round trips and 下 for a quick, light action, so neither counts doses.

q: 今天上午我跑了三___银行，还是没办好。
zh: 今天上午我跑了三趟银行，还是没办好。
py: jīn tiān shàng wǔ wǒ pǎo le sān tàng yín háng hái shi méi bàn hǎo
en: I made three trips to the bank this morning and still haven't got it done.
why: 趟 counts trips there and back. 遍 is for running through something from start to finish, and 下 is for a brief action, not a count of trips.

q: 头有点疼，我想躺___。
zh: 头有点疼，我想躺一下。
py: tóu yǒu diǎn téng wǒ xiǎng tǎng yī xià
en: My head hurts a little; I want to lie down for a moment.
why: 一下 makes a light, brief action: 躺一下. 遍 would mean lying down through something start to finish and 趟 a round trip.

q: 老板要求我把合同从头到尾读___，不能漏掉任何一条。
zh: 老板要求我把合同从头到尾读两遍，不能漏掉任何一条。
py: lǎo bǎn yāo qiú wǒ bǎ hé tong cóng tóu dào wěi dú liǎng biàn bù néng lòu diào rèn hé yī tiáo
en: The boss wants me to read the contract through twice from start to finish, without missing a single clause.
why: 从头到尾 calls for 遍, a whole run-through. 趟 counts trips, and 下 is a quick action that does not count readings.

zh: 他这个星期迟到了三次。
py: tā zhè ge xīng qī chí dào le sān cì
en: He was late three times this week.
why: The count 三次 follows the verb and 了; 这个星期 is a time-when and stays before the verb.

zh: 医生一个星期来两次。
py: yī shēng yī gè xīng qī lái liǎng cì
en: The doctor comes twice a week.
why: The period 一个星期 goes before the verb and only the count 两次 follows it.

zh: 请你再说一遍。
py: qǐng nǐ zài shuō yī biàn
en: Please say it once more.
why: 遍 follows the verb and counts one whole run-through of what is said. 一遍 cannot come before 说.

zh: 我下午要去一趟医院。
py: wǒ xià wǔ yào qù yī tàng yī yuàn
en: I'm going to make a trip to the hospital this afternoon.
why: 趟 counts a trip there and back and follows 去. 下午 is a time-when and stays before the verb. With a place object the count may also follow 医院.

task: Soften it: look for a moment.
zh: 请你看一下这个。
py: qǐng nǐ kàn yī xià zhè ge
en: Please take a look at this.
why: 一下 after the verb softens a request to 'for a moment'. Here it comes before the thing looked at: 看一下这个.

s: 这份合同我从头到尾看了两趟。
s_py: zhè fèn hé tong wǒ cóng tóu dào wěi kàn le liǎng tàng
zh: 这份合同我从头到尾看了两遍。
py: zhè fèn hé tong wǒ cóng tóu dào wěi kàn le liǎng biàn
en: I read this contract through twice from start to finish.
why: 趟 counts trips, so it cannot count readings. Reading a thing through from start to finish is counted with 遍.

s: 我们一个星期开一次会。
s_py: wǒ men yī gè xīng qī kāi yī cì huì
zh: 我们一个星期开一次会。
py: wǒ men yī gè xīng qī kāi yī cì huì
en: We have a meeting once a week.
why: Trap: the period 一个星期 stands before the verb, and only the count 一次 follows it, with the split object 会 last. This is correct.

s: 经理明天要去一遍上海出差。
s_py: jīng lǐ míng tiān yào qù yī biàn shàng hǎi chū chāi
zh: 经理明天要去一趟上海出差。
py: jīng lǐ míng tiān yào qù yī tàng shàng hǎi chū chāi
en: The manager will make a trip to Shanghai on business tomorrow.
why: Going to a place and coming back is counted with 趟. 遍 is for whole run-throughs, so 去一遍 is wrong.

q: 我见过___，他是我们的新经理。
zh: 我见过他一次，他是我们的新经理。
py: wǒ jiàn guo tā yī cì tā shì wǒ men de xīn jīng lǐ
en: I have met him once; he's our new manager.
why: A pronoun object goes before the count: 见过他一次. 见过一次他 is not allowed with 他, 我 or 你.

q: 我跟他只见过一___面，不太熟。
zh: 我跟他只见过一次面，不太熟。
py: wǒ gēn tā zhǐ jiàn guo yī cì miàn bù tài shú
en: I've only met him once; we're not close.
why: 见面 is verb + object and splits around the count: 见过一次面. 遍 and 趟 do not count meetings.

q: 上个月他请了三次___，经理有点不高兴。
zh: 上个月他请了三次假，经理有点不高兴。
py: shàng gè yuè tā qǐng le sān cì jià jīng lǐ yǒu diǎn bù gāo xìng
en: Last month he took leave three times, and the manager is a bit unhappy.
why: 请假 splits around the count: 请了三次假. 请病 and 请班 are not words, so only 假 completes it.

q: 医生给我打了两次___，我的烧才退了。
zh: 医生给我打了两次针，我的烧才退了。
py: yī shēng gěi wǒ dǎ le liǎng cì zhēn wǒ de shāo cái tuì le
en: The doctor gave me two injections before my fever went down.
why: 打针 is the verb-object for giving an injection, so the count goes in the middle: 打了两次针. 打病 and 打汗 are not used this way, and a fever coming down points to an injection.

q: 我在这家医院住过两次___，对这里的医生很熟悉。
zh: 我在这家医院住过两次院，对这里的医生很熟悉。
py: wǒ zài zhè jiā yī yuàn zhù guo liǎng cì yuàn duì zhè lǐ de yī shēng hěn shú xī
en: I have been admitted to this hospital twice, so I know the doctors here well.
why: 住院 is verb + object and splits around 过 and the count: 住过两次院. 住病 and 住医 are not words.

zh: 这份合同我看了三遍。
py: zhè fèn hé tong wǒ kàn le sān biàn
en: I have read this contract three times.
why: A specific thing like 这份合同 is usually moved to the front as the topic, and the count 三遍 follows the verb.

zh: 护士给他量了两次体温。
py: hù shi gěi tā liáng le liǎng cì tǐ wēn
en: The nurse took his temperature twice.
why: A thing object comes after the count: 量了两次体温. The person 他 goes in the 给 phrase before the verb.

zh: 我去过两次上海。
py: wǒ qù guo liǎng cì shàng hǎi
en: I have been to Shanghai twice.
why: With a place object, the count may go on either side: 去过两次上海 or 去过上海两次. Both are fine.

zh: 他今天给我打了三次电话。
py: tā jīn tiān gěi wǒ dǎ le sān cì diàn huà
en: He phoned me three times today.
why: A thing object like 电话 comes after the count: 打了三次电话. 今天 is a time-when and can move before or after 他.

zh: 他一年只请过一次假。
py: tā yī nián zhǐ qǐng guo yī cì jià
en: He takes leave only once a year.
why: 请假 is verb + object, so the count goes between 请过 and 假. The period 一年 stays before the verb.

task: Say you have met him once.
zh: 我见过他一次。
py: wǒ jiàn guo tā yī cì
en: I have met him once.
why: The count 一次 follows the pronoun 他, never precedes it: 见过他一次.

task: Say she has been to the hospital twice.
zh: 她来过医院两次。
py: tā lái guo yī yuàn liǎng cì
en: She has been to the hospital twice.
why: With a place object, the count 两次 can go after the place or before it: both 来过医院两次 and 来过两次医院 are correct.

s: 我在会上见过一次她。
s_py: wǒ zài huì shàng jiàn guo yī cì tā
zh: 我在会上见过她一次。
py: wǒ zài huì shàng jiàn guo tā yī cì
en: I've met her once at a meeting.
why: A pronoun object must come before the count. 见过一次她 puts it after, which is not possible with 她.

s: 我们只见面过一次。
s_py: wǒ men zhǐ jiàn miàn guo yī cì
zh: 我们只见过一次面。
py: wǒ men zhǐ jiàn guo yī cì miàn
en: We have only met once.
why: 见面 is verb + object and cannot take 过 and a count after 面. They go in the middle: 见过一次面.

s: 我看过这个医生两次。
s_py: wǒ kàn guo zhè ge yī shēng liǎng cì
zh: 我看过这个医生两次。
py: wǒ kàn guo zhè ge yī shēng liǎng cì
en: I have seen this doctor twice.
why: Trap: a noun object like 这个医生 can come before the count; only a pronoun must come first. 看过两次这个医生 is also fine.

q: 我昨天晚上___睡觉，睡了八个小时。
zh: 我昨天晚上十一点睡觉，睡了八个小时。
py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang shí yī diǎn shuì jiào shuì le bā gè xiǎo shí
en: I went to bed at eleven last night and slept for eight hours.
why: The clock time 十一点 is a time-when and goes before 睡觉. 十一个小时 is a length and 十一月 is November, so neither fits.

q: 他在这家公司干了___，上个月才辞职。
zh: 他在这家公司干了三年，上个月才辞职。
py: tā zài zhè jiā gōng sī gàn le sān nián shàng gè yuè cái cí zhí
en: He worked at this company for three years and only resigned last month.
why: After 干了 you need a length of time: 三年. 三号 is a date and 三点 a clock time, which tell when and cannot measure how long.

q: 我们___开会，一直开到下午两点半。
zh: 我们上午九点开会，一直开到下午两点半。
py: wǒ men shàng wǔ jiǔ diǎn kāi huì yī zhí kāi dào xià wǔ liǎng diǎn bàn
en: We start the meeting at nine in the morning and it runs until half past two in the afternoon.
why: The start of the meeting is a point in time, so 上午九点 goes before 开会. A length like 九个小时 or 三个小时 does not tell when it begins.

q: 我们的会议星期___开，大家别忘了。
zh: 我们的会议星期三开，大家别忘了。
py: wǒ men de huì yì xīng qī sān kāi dà jiā bié wàng le
en: Our meeting is on Wednesday; everyone, don't forget.
why: 星期三 is a day of the week, a time-when before the verb. 三天 and 三个星期 are lengths and cannot name a weekday.

q: 经理说他下个月要去上海出差，在那儿一共待___。
zh: 经理说他下个月要去上海出差，在那儿一共待两个星期。
py: jīng lǐ shuō tā xià gè yuè yào qù shàng hǎi chū chāi zài nà r yī gòng dāi liǎng gè xīng qī
en: The manager says he's going to Shanghai on business next month and will stay there two weeks in all.
why: How long he stays is a length after the verb: 两个星期. 二月 is February and 两点 is two o'clock, both time-when words.

zh: 我星期六早上七点起床。
py: wǒ xīng qī liù zǎo shang qī diǎn qǐ chuáng
en: I get up at seven on Saturday morning.
why: 星期六早上 and 七点 are both time-when words, so they go before the verb, from the larger unit to the smaller. None of them can follow 起床.

zh: 他星期二下午开了两个小时会。
py: tā xīng qī èr xià wǔ kāi le liǎng gè xiǎo shí huì
en: He was in a meeting for two hours on Tuesday afternoon.
why: 星期二下午 says when and stays before the verb; 两个小时 says how long and sits between 开了 and 会.

zh: 经理三月去北京，在那儿住三个月。
py: jīng lǐ sān yuè qù běi jīng zài nà r zhù sān gè yuè
en: The manager goes to Beijing in March and will stay there for three months.
why: 三月 is March, a time-when before 去; 三个月 is a length of stay after 住. Do not swap them: 三个月 去 and 住 三月 would be wrong.

s: 我昨天晚上睡觉十一点。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang shuì jiào shí yī diǎn
zh: 我昨天晚上十一点睡觉。
py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang shí yī diǎn shuì jiào
en: I went to bed at eleven last night.
why: 十一点 says when, so it belongs before the verb. After 睡觉 it would have to be a length, and 十一点 is not one.

s: 他在医院住了三月。
s_py: tā zài yī yuàn zhù le sān yuè
zh: 他在医院住了三个月。
py: tā zài yī yuàn zhù le sān gè yuè
en: He stayed in the hospital for three months.
why: 三月 is March. A length of three months must be 三个月, with 个, and it follows 住了.

s: 我下午两点开会，要开两个小时。
s_py: wǒ xià wǔ liǎng diǎn kāi huì yào kāi liǎng gè xiǎo shí
zh: 我下午两点开会，要开两个小时。
py: wǒ xià wǔ liǎng diǎn kāi huì yào kāi liǎng gè xiǎo shí
en: I have a meeting at two in the afternoon, and it will take two hours.
why: Trap: the time-when 下午两点 is before the verb and the length 两个小时 after it. Each sits in its own slot, so this is correct.

s: 我去年在这家公司实习了三个月。
s_py: wǒ qù nián zài zhè jiā gōng sī shí xí le sān gè yuè
zh: 我去年在这家公司实习了三个月。
py: wǒ qù nián zài zhè jiā gōng sī shí xí le sān gè yuè
en: Last year I did an internship at this company for three months.
why: Trap: 去年 (when) comes before the verb and 三个月 (how long) after 实习了. Two time words in one sentence are fine when they fill different slots.

s: 为了准备这个报告，我昨天晚上三个小时加班了。
s_py: wèi le zhǔn bèi zhè ge bào gào wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang sān gè xiǎo shí jiā bān le
zh: 为了准备这个报告，我昨天晚上加了三个小时班。
py: wèi le zhǔn bèi zhè ge bào gào wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang jiā le sān gè xiǎo shí bān
en: I worked overtime for three hours last night to prepare this report.
why: 三个小时 is a length, not a time-when, so it cannot stand before 加班. It goes between 加了 and 班.
